title: Therms and CCF: How Natural Gas Is Billed
h1: Therms, CCF, MMBtu — reading a natural-gas bill
description: US gas utilities bill in therms or CCF. Neither is a familiar unit. Here is what they mean and how to convert to kWh or MJ.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

hero: A therm is 100,000 BTU. A CCF is 100 cubic feet of gas. They are not the same, and both appear on the same bill.
body: US gas utilities measure gas delivery by volume (cubic feet) but bill by energy (therms or dekatherms). The conversion depends on the heating value of the specific gas mix delivered — typically 1,020 to 1,040 BTU per cubic foot for pipeline natural gas.

> 1 therm = 100,000 BTU = 105.51 MJ = 29.30 kWh
> 1 CCF = 100 ft³ ≈ 1.037 therms (varies by heating value)
> 1 MCF = 1,000 ft³ ≈ 10.37 therms = 1.037 MMBtu
> 1 dekatherm (dth) = 10 therms = 1.055 GJ
## Why two units on one bill

The meter measures cubic feet (volume). The utility multiplies by the current heating value to get therms. Both usually appear on the bill: 'Used: 45 CCF × 1.033 therms/CCF = 46.5 therms'. Rates are almost always quoted per therm, not per CCF, because heating value varies month to month.

UK and EU bills: kWh directly. Meter is read in m³, utility multiplies by the local calorific value (~11 kWh/m³) to get kWh. Canada: gigajoules (GJ). Australia: MJ. The US therm/CCF convention is unique to North America.

100 therms × 29.30 = 2,930 kWh of heat. If burned in an 80% efficient furnace: 2,344 kWh of usable heat delivered to the house. At $1.20/therm (2025 US average), monthly bill: $120. Compare to electric resistance heat at $0.16/kWh: 2,344 kWh × $0.16 = $375 for the same delivered heat — over 3× more.

A modern cold-climate heat pump has COP ~3 in winter. That 2,344 kWh of delivered heat requires only 780 kWh of electricity = $125 at $0.16/kWh — competitive with gas even in expensive electricity markets. This is why heat-pump adoption is accelerating in gas-heated regions.
1 therm = 100,000 BTU = 29.3 kWh = 105.5 MJ. 1 CCF ≈ 1 therm (varies). Divide gas bill by heating value to compare with electric bills.

faqs.a: It is short for 'thermie' — a legacy French metric unit. The US therm (100,000 BTU) is unrelated to the French 'thermie' (1 Mcal).

faqs.q: Is CCF the same as MCF?
faqs.a: No. CCF = 100 cubic feet (one 'C' is Roman 100). MCF = 1,000 cubic feet (one 'M' is Roman 1,000). Confusion between them is common on commercial invoices.
Pipeline gas is mostly methane but includes 2–10% ethane, propane and inerts. The mix varies with supply source and season.
